items.title: CAC Consortium: high coronary calcium in adults aged 30-45 linked to higher mortality over long-term follow-up (JAMA Cardiology)
items.summary: In 12,847 adults aged 30 to 45 who had clinically indicated CAC scans, a CAC score above the 90th percentile was linked to about 1.9 to 3.7 times higher all-cause, cardiovascular and coronary mortality over a median 22.6-year follow-up (JAMA Cardiology, Oct 23, 2026).
bullets: **CAC Consortium** (JAMA Cardiology, Oct 2026): long-term mortality with **coronary artery calcium (CAC)** in **young adults aged 30-45**.
**12,847 participants**, mean age **40.5**, **77.2% male**; median follow-up **22.6 years**; **624 deaths** (149 CVD, 81 CHD).
Modelled **30-year mortality** (>90th percentile vs 0): all-cause **12.9% vs 7.5%**, CVD **4.5% vs 1.5%**, CHD **3.0% vs 0.6%**.

Authors' message: CAC >90th percentile in a young adult marks a **high-risk phenotype** and may **help guide earlier, more intensive prevention**; it does not show that acting on it improves outcomes.
Caveats: **retrospective referral cohort**, mostly men, long-term risks are **modelled**.
items.source: Choi S, ... Blaha MJ. JAMA Cardiol, Oct 23, 2026. doi:10.1001/jamacardio.2026.4819
